Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.

# Fizzy

This is the source code of [Fizzy](https://fizzy.do/), the Kanban tracking tool for issues and ideas by [37signals](https://37signals.com).


## Running your own Fizzy instance

If you want to run your own Fizzy instance, but don't need to change its code, you can use our pre-built Docker image.
You'll need access to a server on which you can run Docker, and you'll need to configure some options to customize your installation.

You can find the details of how to do a Docker-based deployment in our [Docker deployment guide](docs/docker-deployment.md).

If you want more flexibility to customize your Fizzy installation by changing its code, and deploy those changes to your server, then we recommend you deploy Fizzy with Kamal. You can find a complete walkthrough of doing that in our [Kamal deployment guide](docs/kamal-deployment.md).


## Development

You are welcome -- and encouraged -- to modify Fizzy to your liking.
Please see our [Development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Fizzy set up for local development.


## Contributing

We welcome contributions! Please read our [style guide](STYLE.md) before submitting code.


## License

Fizzy is released under the [O'Saasy License](LICENSE.md).

# How to contribute to Fizzy

Fizzy uses GitHub
[discussions](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/discussions) to track
feature requests and questions, rather than [the issue
tracker](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/issues). If you're considering
opening an issue or pull request, please open a discussion instead.

Whenever a discussion leads to an actionable and well-understood task, we'll
move it to the issue tracker where it can be worked on.

This is a little different than how some other projects work, but it makes it
easier for us to triage and prioritise the work. It also means that the open
issues all represent agreed-upon tasks that are either being worked on, or are
ready to be worked on.

This should also make it easier to see what's in progress, and to find
something to work on if you'd like to do so.

## What this means in practice

### If you'd like to contribute to the code...

1. If you're interested in working on one of the open issues, please do! We are
   grateful for the help!
2. You'll want to make sure someone else isn't already working on the same
   issue. If they are, it will be tagged "in progress" and/or it should be clear
   from the comments. When in doubt, you can always comment on the issue to ask.
3. Similarly, if you need any help or guidance on the issue, please comment on
   the issue as you go, and we'll do our best to help.
4. When you have something ready for review or collaboration, open a PR.

### If you've found a bug...

1. If you don't have steps to reproduce the problem, or you're not certain it's a
   bug, open a discussion.
2. If you have steps to reproduce, open an issue.

### If you have an idea for a feature...

1. Open a discussion.

### If you have a question, or are having trouble with configuration...

1. Open a discussion.

Hopefully this process makes it easier for everyone to be involved. Thanks for
helping! ❤️

Deploy: `bin/kamal deploy -d <destination>`

This is a Rails engine that [37signals](https://37signals.com/) bundles with [Fizzy](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy) to offer the hosted version at https://fizzy.do.

## Development

To make Fizzy run in SaaS mode, run this in the terminal:

```ruby
bin/rails saas:enable
```

To go back to open source mode:

```ruby
bin/rails saas:disable
```

Then you can do [Fizzy development as usual](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy).

## How to update Fizzy

After making changes to this gem, you need to update Fizzy to pick up the changes:

```ruby
BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.saas bundle update --conservative fizzy-saas
```

## Working with Stripe

The first time, you need to:

1. Install Stripe CLI: https://stripe.com/docs/stripe-cli
2. Run `stripe login` and authorize the environment `37signals Development`

Then, for working on the Stripe integration locally, you need to run this script to start the tunneling and set the environment variables:

```sh
eval "$(BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.saas bundle exec stripe-dev)"
bin/dev # You need to start the dev server in the same terminal session
```

This will ask for your 1password authorization to read and set the environment variables that Stripe needs.

### Stripe environments

* [Development](https://dashboard.stripe.com/acct_1SdTFtRus34tgjsJ/test/dashboard)
* [Staging](https://dashboard.stripe.com/acct_1SdTbuRvb8txnPBR/test/dashboard)
* [Production](https://dashboard.stripe.com/acct_1SNy97RwChFE4it8/dashboard)

## Working with Push Notifications

To test native push notifications (APNs and FCM) locally, start the dev server with the `--push` flag:

```sh
bin/dev --push
```

This will ask for your 1Password authorization to fetch the push credentials. Note that this loads the **production** APNs and FCM credentials into your environment.

## Environments

Fizzy is deployed with [Kamal](https://kamal-deploy.org/). You'll need to have the 1Password CLI set up in order to access the secrets that are used when deploying. Provided you have that, it should be as simple as `bin/kamal deploy` to the correct environment.

## Handbook

See the [Fizzy handbook](https://handbooks.37signals.works/18/fizzy) for runbooks and more.

### Production

- https://app.fizzy.do/

This environment uses a FlashBlade bucket for blob storage.

### Beta

Beta is primarily intended for testing product features. It uses the same production database and Active Storage configuration.

There is 1 beta environment:

- https://beta1.fizzy-beta.com

Deploy with: `bin/kamal deploy -d beta1`

### Staging

Staging is primarily intended for testing infrastructure changes. It uses production-like but separate database and Active Storage configurations.

- https://app.fizzy-staging.com/

module Account::StorageLimited
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT = 1.gigabyte
  NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 500.megabytes

  included do
    has_one :storage_exception
  end

  def storage_limit
    storage_exception&.bytes_allowed || DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT
  end

  def exceeding_storage_limit?
    bytes_used > storage_limit
  end

  def nearing_storage_limit?
    !exceeding_storage_limit? && bytes_used > storage_limit - NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end

  def add_storage_exception(bytes)
    if storage_exception
      storage_exception.update!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    else
      create_storage_exception!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    end
  end
end

# Local stand-in for the private queenbee billing client. Reconstructs the
# public surface Fizzy touches: host-app registration, the Client concern,
# the Subscription property DSL, the remote Account resource, and the API
# token holder. No network calls happen unless Remote::Account is used.
require "active_support"
require "active_support/core_ext"

module Queenbee
  singleton_class.attr_accessor :host_app

  # The private gem draws its account-management API here; the stand-in has
  # no remote counterpart to serve, so there is nothing to draw.
  def self.routes(mapper)
  end

  class ApiToken
    singleton_class.attr_accessor :token
  end

  module Client
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    def qb_serializable_hash
      { id: queenbee_id, subscription: { quantity: 1 } }
    end
  end

  class Subscription
    singleton_class.attr_accessor :short_names

    def self.property(name, value)
      properties[name] = value
      define_method(name) { value }
      define_singleton_method(name) { value }
    end

    def self.properties
      @properties ||= superclass.respond_to?(:properties) ? superclass.properties.dup : {}
    end
  end

  module Remote
    class Account
      class << self
        def create!(attributes)
          new(attributes)
        end

        def find(*)
          raise NotImplementedError, "Queenbee remote lookups are not available here"
        end
      end

      attr_reader :attributes

      def initialize(attributes = {})
        @attributes = attributes.with_indifferent_access
      end

      def id = attributes[:id]

      def method_missing(name, *args)
        attributes.key?(name) ? attributes[name] : super
      end

      def respond_to_missing?(name, include_private = false)
        attributes.key?(name) || super
      end
    end
  end

class Storage::Entry < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :board, optional: true
  belongs_to :recordable, polymorphic: true, optional: true

  scope :pending, ->(last_entry_id) { where.not(id: ..last_entry_id) if last_entry_id }

  thread_mattr_accessor :recording, default: true

  def self.suppressing_recording(&block)
    original, self.recording = self.recording, false
    yield
  ensure
    self.recording = original
  end

  # Records may be destroyed (during cascading deletes) but .id still works.
  # Skip entirely if account is destroyed - no need to track storage for deleted accounts.
  # Skip materialize jobs for destroyed boards since there's nothing to update.
  def self.record(delta:, operation:, account:, board: nil, recordable: nil, blob: nil)
    return if delta.zero?
    return if account.destroyed?
    return unless recording

    entry = create! \
      account_id: account.id,
      board_id: board&.id,
      recordable_type: recordable&.class&.name,
      recordable_id: recordable&.id,
      blob_id: blob&.id,
      delta: delta,
      operation: operation,
      user_id: Current.user&.id,
      request_id: Current.request_id

    account.materialize_storage_later
    board&.materialize_storage_later unless board&.destroyed?

    entry
  end
end

module Storage::AttachmentTracking
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    # Snapshot IDs in before_destroy since parent record may be deleted
    # by the time after_destroy_commit runs
    before_destroy :snapshot_storage_context
    after_create_commit :record_storage_attach
    after_destroy_commit :record_storage_detach
  end

  private
    def record_storage_attach
      return unless storage_tracked_record

      Storage::Entry.record \
        account: storage_tracked_record.account,
        board: storage_tracked_record.board_for_storage_tracking,
        recordable: storage_tracked_record,
        blob: blob,
        delta: blob.byte_size,
        operation: "attach"
    end

    def record_storage_detach
      return unless @storage_snapshot

      Storage::Entry.record \
        account: @storage_snapshot[:account],
        board: @storage_snapshot[:board],
        recordable: @storage_snapshot[:recordable],
        blob: blob,
        delta: -blob.byte_size,
        operation: "detach"
    end

    # Snapshot records in before_destroy since parent may be deleted by the time
    # after_destroy_commit runs. The records may be destroyed but .id still works.
    def snapshot_storage_context
      return unless storage_tracked_record

      @storage_snapshot = {
        account: storage_tracked_record.account,
        board: storage_tracked_record.board_for_storage_tracking,
        recordable: storage_tracked_record
      }
    end

    def storage_tracked_record
      record.try(:storage_tracked_record)
    end
end

module Storage::Totaled
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_one :storage_total, as: :owner, class_name: "Storage::Total", dependent: :destroy
    has_many :storage_entries, class_name: "Storage::Entry", foreign_key: foreign_key_for_storage
  end

  class_methods do
    def foreign_key_for_storage
      "#{model_name.singular}_id"
    end
  end

  # Fast: materialized snapshot (may be slightly stale)
  def bytes_used
    storage_total&.bytes_stored || 0
  end

  # Exact: snapshot + pending entries
  def bytes_used_exact
    create_or_find_storage_total.current_usage
  end

  def materialize_storage_later
    Storage::MaterializeJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  # Materialize all pending entries into snapshot
  def materialize_storage
    total = create_or_find_storage_total

    total.with_lock do
      latest_entry_id = storage_entries.maximum(:id)

      if latest_entry_id && total.last_entry_id != latest_entry_id
        scope = storage_entries.where(id: ..latest_entry_id)
        scope = scope.where.not(id: ..total.last_entry_id) if total.last_entry_id
        delta_sum = scope.sum(:delta)

        total.update! bytes_stored: total.bytes_stored + delta_sum, last_entry_id: latest_entry_id
      end
    end
  end

  # Reconcile ledger against actual attachment storage.
  #
  # Uses two-cursor approach for consistency: capture cursor before AND after the
  # scan. If they differ, entries were added during the scan and we can't get an
  # accurate diff without risking double-counting or undercounting.
  #
  # Returns true if reconciled successfully, false if aborted due to concurrent
  # writes. Caller (ReconcileJob) handles retries to avoid amplification.
  def reconcile_storage
    cursor_before = storage_entries.maximum(:id)
    real_bytes = calculate_real_storage_bytes
    cursor_after = storage_entries.maximum(:id)

    if cursor_before != cursor_after
      Rails.logger.warn "[Storage] Reconcile aborted for #{self.class}##{id}: cursor moved during scan"
      false
    else
      ledger_bytes = cursor_after ? storage_entries.where(id: ..cursor_after).sum(:delta) : 0
      diff = real_bytes - ledger_bytes

      if diff.nonzero?
        Rails.logger.info "[Storage] Reconcile #{self.class}##{id}: adjusting by #{diff} bytes"
        Storage::Entry.record \
          account: is_a?(Account) ? self : account,
          board: is_a?(Board) ? self : nil,
          recordable: nil,
          delta: diff,
          operation: "reconcile"
      end

      true
    end
  end

  private
    def create_or_find_storage_total
      self.storage_total ||= Storage::Total.create_or_find_by!(owner: self)
    end

    def calculate_real_storage_bytes
      raise NotImplementedError, "Subclass must implement calculate_real_storage_bytes"
    end
end

require "test_helper"
require "queenbee/testing/client"

class Account::QueenbeeIntegrationTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include Queenbee::Testing::Client

  # Fizzy creates accounts via its own Signup flow (Fizzy → Queenbee),
  # not via Queenbee pushing to Fizzy, so create_with_dependents is N/A.
  undef_method :test_client_class_should_respond_to_create_with_dependents

  setup do
    @account = accounts(:"37s")
  end

  test "find_by_queenbee_id looks up by external_account_id" do
    assert_equal @account, Account.find_by_queenbee_id(@account.external_account_id)
  end

  test "queenbee_id returns external_account_id" do
    assert_equal @account.external_account_id, @account.queenbee_id
  end

  test "cancel! creates cancellation attributed to system user" do
    @account.cancel!

    assert @account.cancelled?
    assert_equal @account.system_user, @account.cancellation.initiated_by
  end

  test "cancel! is idempotent" do
    @account.cancel!
    assert_no_difference -> { Account::Cancellation.count } do
      @account.cancel!
    end
  end

  test "cancel and reactivate round-trips" do
    @account.cancel!
    assert_not @account.active?

    @account.reactivate!
    @account.reload
    assert @account.active?
  end

  test "deactivate! cancels the account" do
    @account.deactivate!
    assert @account.cancelled?
  end

  test "owner_name and owner_email from account owner" do
    assert_equal users(:jason).name, @account.owner_name
    assert_equal "jason@37signals.com", @account.owner_email
  end

  test "comped= is a no-op" do
    @account.comped = true
    assert_not @account.comped?
  end

  test "transferred_ownership! raises NotImplementedError" do
    assert_raises(NotImplementedError) { @account.transferred_ownership! }
  end

  test "qb_serializable_hash includes queenbee_id and subscription" do
    hash = @account.qb_serializable_hash
    assert_equal @account.external_account_id, hash[:id]
    assert_equal({ quantity: 1 }, hash[:subscription])
  end
end

class Account::StorageLimitedTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase

  end

  test "nearing storage limit when within 500 MB of the limit" do

require "test_helper"

class Account::StorageExceptionTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "storage limit returns default when no exception exists" do
    assert_equal Account::StorageLimited::DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT, accounts(:initech).storage_limit
  end

  test "storage limit returns exception value when one exists" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    account.add_storage_exception(5.gigabytes)

    assert_equal 5.gigabytes, account.storage_limit
  end

  test "add storage exception creates a new record" do
    account = accounts(:initech)

    assert_difference -> { Account::StorageException.count } do
      account.add_storage_exception(2.gigabytes)
    end

    assert_equal 2.gigabytes, account.storage_exception.bytes_allowed
  end

  test "add storage exception updates existing record" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    account.add_storage_exception(2.gigabytes)

    assert_no_difference -> { Account::StorageException.count } do
      account.add_storage_exception(10.gigabytes)
    end

    assert_equal 10.gigabytes, account.storage_exception.reload.bytes_allowed
  end

  test "exceeding storage limit respects exception" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    Account.any_instance.stubs(:bytes_used).returns(2.gigabytes)

    assert account.exceeding_storage_limit?

    account.add_storage_exception(5.gigabytes)

    assert_not account.exceeding_storage_limit?
  end
end

  PATTERN = /(\d+)/
  PATH_INFO_MATCH = /\A(\/#{AccountSlug::PATTERN})/

  class Extractor
    def initialize(app)
      @app = app
    end

    # We're using account id prefixes in the URL path. Rather than namespace
    # all our routes, we're "mounting" the Rails app at this URL prefix.
    def call(env)
      request = ActionDispatch::Request.new(env)

      # $1, $2, $' == script_name, slug, path_info
      if request.script_name && request.script_name =~ PATH_INFO_MATCH
        # Likely due to restarting the action cable connection after upgrade
        env["fizzy.external_account_id"] = AccountSlug.decode($2)
      elsif request.path_info =~ PATH_INFO_MATCH
        # Yanks the prefix off PATH_INFO and move it to SCRIPT_NAME
        request.engine_script_name = request.script_name = $1
        request.path_info   = $'.empty? ? "/" : $'

        # Stash the account's Queenbee ID.
        env["fizzy.external_account_id"] = AccountSlug.decode($2)
      end

      if env["fizzy.external_account_id"]
        account = Account.find_by(external_account_id: env["fizzy.external_account_id"])
        Current.with_account(account) do
          @app.call env
        end
      else
        Current.without_account do
          @app.call env
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def self.decode(slug) slug.to_i end
  def self.encode(id) id.to_s end
end

Rails.application.config.middleware.insert_after Rack::TempfileReaper, AccountSlug::Extractor

module User::Role
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    enum :role, %i[ owner admin member system ].index_by(&:itself), scopes: false

    scope :owner, -> { where(active: true, role: :owner) }
    scope :admin, -> { where(active: true, role: %i[ owner admin ]) }
    scope :member, -> { where(active: true, role: :member) }
    scope :active, -> { where(active: true, role: %i[ owner admin member ]) }

    def admin?
      super || owner?
    end
  end

  def can_change?(other)
    (admin? && !other.owner?) || other == self
  end

  def can_administer?(other)
    admin? && !other.owner? && other != self
  end

  def can_administer_board?(board)
    admin? || board.creator == self
  end

  def can_administer_card?(card)
    admin? || card.creator == self
  end
end

class Signup
  include ActiveModel::Model
  include ActiveModel::Attributes
  include ActiveModel::Validations

  attr_accessor :full_name, :email_address, :identity, :skip_account_seeding
  attr_reader :account, :user

  validates :email_address, format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP }, on: :identity_creation
  validates :full_name, :identity, presence: true, on: :completion
  validates :full_name, length: { maximum: 240 }

  def initialize(...)
    super

    @email_address = @identity.email_address if @identity
  end

  def create_identity
    @identity = Identity.find_or_create_by!(email_address: email_address)
    @identity.send_magic_link for: :sign_up
  end

  def complete
    if valid?(:completion)
      begin
        @tenant = create_tenant
        create_account
        true
      rescue => error
        destroy_account
        handle_account_creation_error(error)

        errors.add(:base, "Something went wrong, and we couldn't create your account. Please give it another try.")
        Rails.error.report(error, severity: :error)
        Rails.logger.error error
        Rails.logger.error error.backtrace.join("\n")

        false
      end

steps.message:
I have enough context to design this. Before writing code, here's the plan I'm going with:

- **Plans** (`Plan`): Free (1,000 published cards, 1 GB), Unlimited ($20, 5 GB), Unlimited+ ($25, 500 GB). A plan comes from an entitled Stripe subscription. Comp grants Unlimited without one. Otherwise the account is Free.
- **Limits**: card count is published cards. Overrides replace the measured card count and bytes used. The existing per-account `StorageException` still wins over plan storage.
- **Stripe**: a single gateway wraps Checkout, the Billing Portal, cancellation, and webhook verification. The webhook upserts `AccountSubscription` by Stripe subscription ID and ignores stale events.
- **Enforcement**: out-of-cards blocks publish and JSON create. Drafts still work. The footer swaps create buttons for an upgrade pitch and shows "N cards left" from 100 out.
- **Admin**: `/admin/accounts`, account page, Comp/Uncomp, Override, and Reset.

steps.message: The dump also rewrote unrelated tables by adding `limit: 255` noise. I'll restore the original file and splice in only the three new tables and the version bump, so the diff stays limited to billing.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > /tmp/splice_schema.rb <<'EOF'
# Splices only the restored billing tables (and the version bump) from a fresh
# dump into the committed schema file, leaving unrelated tables untouched.
TABLES = %w[account_billing_waivers account_overridden_limits account_subscriptions]

def blocks(text)
  text.scan(/^  create_table "([^"]+)".*?^  end\n\n?/m).each_with_object({}) { |(name), h| }
  result = {}
  text.scan(/^  create_table "([^"]+)".*?^  end\n/m) { result[$1] = $& }
  result
end

fresh = File.read(ARGV[0])
committed = File.read(ARGV[1])

fresh_blocks = blocks(fresh)
committed_blocks = blocks(committed)

# Drop committed table blocks for our tables, then insert the fresh versions in name order.
TABLES.each { |t| committed = committed.sub(committed_blocks[t], "") if committed_blocks[t] }
committed = committed.sub(/define\(version: \d+_\d+_\d+_\d+\)/, "define(version: 2026_04_20_000000)")

TABLES.each do |t|
  block = fresh_blocks.fetch(t)
  # insert before the first existing table whose name sorts after t
  names = committed.scan(/^  create_table "([^"]+)"/).flatten
  nxt = names.find { |n| n > t }
  if nxt
    committed = committed.sub(/^  create_table "#{Regexp.escape(nxt)}"/) { block + "\n" + $& }
  else
    committed = committed.sub(/^end\s*\z/) { block + "\n" + $& }
  end
end

File.write(ARGV[1], committed)
EOF

# Hosted Fizzy plans. Every account starts on Free. A paid plan comes from an

class Plan
  attr_reader :key, :name, :monthly_price, :card_limit, :storage_limit, :queenbee_short_name

  # Environment variable holding the Stripe price for this plan, if it's paid.
  attr_reader :stripe_price_env

  def initialize(key:, name:, monthly_price:, card_limit:, storage_limit:, queenbee_short_name:, stripe_price_env: nil)

    @storage_limit = storage_limit
    @queenbee_short_name = queenbee_short_name
    @stripe_price_env = stripe_price_env
  end

  # nil card_limit means unlimited cards.

    name: "Free",

# One row per Stripe subscription. Stripe is the source of truth; these rows are
# kept in sync by the webhook at /stripe/webhooks.
class AccountSubscription < SaasRecord
  # Stripe statuses that keep the account on its paid plan. past_due stays
  # entitled while Stripe retries the card.
  ENTITLED_STATUSES = %w[ active trialing past_due ].freeze

  belongs_to :account

  validates :plan_key, :stripe_customer_id, :stripe_subscription_id, :status, presence: true

  scope :entitled, -> { where(status: ENTITLED_STATUSES) }
  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  class << self
    # Applies a customer.subscription.* event. Events older than the last one
    # applied are ignored, so out-of-order delivery can't roll a plan back.
    def sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription, event_at:)
      record = find_or_initialize_by(stripe_subscription_id: stripe_subscription.id)
      return record if record.stripe_event_at && event_at < record.stripe_event_at

      account = record.account || Account.find_by(id: metadata_value(stripe_subscription, :account_id))
      plan = Plan.for_stripe_price(price_id_of(stripe_subscription))
      plan_key = plan&.key || record.plan_key

      if account.nil? || plan_key.nil?
        Rails.logger.warn "[Billing] Ignoring Stripe subscription #{stripe_subscription.id}: unknown account or price"
        return
      end

      record.update!(
        account: account,
        plan_key: plan_key,
        stripe_customer_id: customer_id_of(stripe_subscription),
        status: stripe_subscription[:status],
        current_period_end: current_period_end_of(stripe_subscription),
        cancel_at: timestamp_of(stripe_subscription[:cancel_at]),
        stripe_event_at: event_at
      )
      record
    end

    private
      def metadata_value(stripe_subscription, key)
        metadata = stripe_subscription[:metadata]
        metadata[key] if metadata
      end

      def first_item_of(stripe_subscription)
        stripe_subscription[:items]&.data&.first
      end

      def price_id_of(stripe_subscription)
        first_item_of(stripe_subscription)&.price&.id
      end

      def customer_id_of(stripe_subscription)
        customer = stripe_subscription[:customer]
        customer.respond_to?(:id) ? customer.id : customer
      end

      # The period end lives on the subscription item in current Stripe API
      # versions and on the subscription in older ones.
      def current_period_end_of(stripe_subscription)
        timestamp_of(stripe_subscription[:current_period_end] || first_item_of(stripe_subscription)&.current_period_end)
      end

      def timestamp_of(seconds)
        Time.zone.at(seconds) if seconds
      end
  end

  def plan
    Plan.find(plan_key)
  end

  def entitled?
    ENTITLED_STATUSES.include?(status)
  end
end

# Which plan an account is on, and the support-side comp that grants one.
module Account::Billing
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :account_subscriptions

    set_callback :cancel, :after, :cancel_stripe_subscriptions
  end

  def current_plan
    if subscription = active_subscription
      subscription.plan
    elsif comped?
      Plan::UNLIMITED
    else
      Plan::FREE
    end
  end

  def active_subscription
    account_subscriptions.entitled.newest_first.first
  end

  def stripe_customer_id
    account_subscriptions.newest_first.pick(:stripe_customer_id)
  end

  def paid_plan?
    current_plan.paid?
  end

  def comped?
    Account::BillingWaiver.exists?(account_id: id)
  end

  def comp!
    Account::BillingWaiver.find_or_create_by!(account_id: id)
  end

  def uncomp!
    Account::BillingWaiver.where(account_id: id).delete_all
  end

  private
    # Cancelling an account ends its subscriptions. Stripe runs in a job so a
    # Stripe outage can't hold up the cancellation transaction.
    def cancel_stripe_subscriptions
      account_subscriptions.entitled.pluck(:stripe_subscription_id).each do |stripe_subscription_id|
        StripeSubscriptionCancellationJob.perform_later(stripe_subscription_id)
      end
    end
end

# Support overrides for the card count and bytes used that limits are checked against.
module Account::LimitOverrides
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  def overridden_limit
    Account::OverriddenLimit.find_by(account_id: id)
  end

  def effective_card_count
    overridden_limit&.card_count || cards.published.count
  end

  def effective_bytes_used
    overridden_limit&.bytes_used || bytes_used
  end

  # Blank values mean no override for that field. Both blank removes the override.
  def override_limits!(card_count:, bytes_used:)
    card_count = card_count.presence
    bytes_used = bytes_used.presence

    if card_count.nil? && bytes_used.nil?
      reset_limit_overrides!
    else
      Account::OverriddenLimit.find_or_initialize_by(account_id: id).update!(card_count: card_count, bytes_used: bytes_used)
    end
  end

  def reset_limit_overrides!
    Account::OverriddenLimit.where(account_id: id).delete_all
  end
end

# Card allowance for the account's plan. Only published cards count; drafts are
# always allowed.
module Account::CardLimited
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  NEAR_CARD_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 100

  def card_limit
    current_plan.card_limit
  end

  def cards_remaining
    card_limit - effective_card_count if card_limit
  end

  # Out of cards means the next published card would go over the limit.
  def out_of_cards?
    card_limit.present? && cards_remaining <= 0
  end

  def nearing_card_limit?
    return false unless card_limit

    remaining = cards_remaining
    remaining.positive? && remaining <= NEAR_CARD_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end
end
EOF

module Account::StorageLimited
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT = Plan::FREE.storage_limit
  NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 500.megabytes

  included do
    has_one :storage_exception
  end

  # A per-account exception wins over the plan's allowance.
  def storage_limit
    storage_exception&.bytes_allowed || current_plan.storage_limit
  end

  def exceeding_storage_limit?
    effective_bytes_used > storage_limit
  end

  def nearing_storage_limit?
    !exceeding_storage_limit? && effective_bytes_used > storage_limit - NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end

  def add_storage_exception(bytes)
    if storage_exception
      storage_exception.update!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    else
      create_storage_exception!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    end
  end
end

# The only code that calls Stripe. Checkout and the customer portal are hosted by
# Stripe, so this only creates their sessions, cancels subscriptions, and verifies
# webhook signatures.
module StripeGateway
  class PlanUnavailable < StandardError; end

  class << self
    def configure!
      Stripe.api_key = ENV["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"]
    end

    def checkout_url(account:, plan:, success_url:, cancel_url:)
      raise PlanUnavailable, "No Stripe price is configured for #{plan.name}" unless plan.stripe_price_id

      params = {
        mode: "subscription",
        line_items: [ { price: plan.stripe_price_id, quantity: 1 } ],
        client_reference_id: account.id,
        metadata: { account_id: account.id },
        subscription_data: { metadata: { account_id: account.id } },
        success_url: success_url,
        cancel_url: cancel_url
      }

      # Reuse the customer so an account that subscribes again keeps one Stripe customer.
      if customer_id = account.stripe_customer_id
        params[:customer] = customer_id
      end

      Stripe::Checkout::Session.create(params).url
    end

    def billing_portal_url(customer_id:, return_url:)
      Stripe::BillingPortal::Session.create(customer: customer_id, return_url: return_url).url
    end

    def cancel_subscription(stripe_subscription_id)
      Stripe::Subscription.cancel(stripe_subscription_id)
    end

    # Raises Stripe::SignatureVerificationError or JSON::ParserError for a bad request.
    def construct_event(payload, signature_header)
      Stripe::Webhook.construct_event(payload, signature_header, webhook_secret)
    end

    def webhook_secret
      ENV["STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"].presence
    end
  end
end
EOF

# Cancels a Stripe subscription when its account is cancelled.
class StripeSubscriptionCancellationJob < ApplicationJob
  retry_on Stripe::APIConnectionError, wait: 1.minute, attempts: 5

  def perform(stripe_subscription_id)
    StripeGateway.cancel_subscription(stripe_subscription_id)
  rescue Stripe::InvalidRequestError => error
    # Already cancelled or gone in Stripe, so there's nothing left to do.
    Rails.logger.info "[Billing] Stripe subscription #{stripe_subscription_id} not cancelled: #{error.message}"
  end
end
EOF

# Stripe posts subscription changes here. Requests come from Stripe rather than a
# browser, so there is no session, CSRF token, or account slug.
class StripeWebhooksController < ActionController::Base
  skip_forgery_protection

  SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS = %w[
    customer.subscription.created
    customer.subscription.updated
    customer.subscription.deleted
  ].freeze

  def create
    # Without the secret the signature can't be checked. Fail with a 500 so Stripe retries once it's configured.
    unless StripeGateway.webhook_secret
      Rails.logger.error "[Billing] STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set; rejecting webhook"
      return head :internal_server_error
    end

    event = StripeGateway.construct_event(request.raw_post, request.headers["Stripe-Signature"])

    if SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS.include?(event.type)
      AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(event.data.object, event_at: Time.zone.at(event.created))
    end

    head :ok
  rescue JSON::ParserError, Stripe::SignatureVerificationError
    head :bad_request
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class PlanTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "free plan allows 1,000 cards and 1 GB" do
    assert_equal 1_000, Plan::FREE.card_limit
    assert_equal 1.gigabyte, Plan::FREE.storage_limit
    assert_not Plan::FREE.paid?
  end

  test "unlimited plan is $20/month with unlimited cards and 5 GB" do
    assert_predicate Plan::UNLIMITED, :unlimited_cards?
    assert_equal 5.gigabytes, Plan::UNLIMITED.storage_limit
    assert_equal "$20/month", Plan::UNLIMITED.price_label
    assert_predicate Plan::UNLIMITED, :paid?
  end

  test "unlimited plus is $25/month with unlimited cards and 500 GB" do
    assert_predicate Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS, :unlimited_cards?
    assert_equal 500.gigabytes, Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS.storage_limit
    assert_equal "$25/month", Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS.price_label
  end

  test "allowances read well on the plan page" do
    assert_equal "1,000 cards", Plan::FREE.card_allowance
    assert_equal "Unlimited cards", Plan::UNLIMITED.card_allowance
    assert_equal "1 GB", Plan::FREE.storage_allowance
    assert_equal "500 GB", Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS.storage_allowance
  end

  test "find and find_paid look plans up by key" do
    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED, Plan.find("unlimited")
    assert_nil Plan.find("gold")
    assert_nil Plan.find_paid("free")
    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS, Plan.find_paid("unlimited_plus")
  end

  test "for_stripe_price maps configured price ids to paid plans" do
    Plan::UNLIMITED.stubs(:stripe_price_id).returns("price_unlimited")
    Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS.stubs(:stripe_price_id).returns("price_unlimited_plus")

    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED, Plan.for_stripe_price("price_unlimited")
    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS, Plan.for_stripe_price("price_unlimited_plus")
    assert_nil Plan.for_stripe_price("price_something_else")
  end

  test "for_stripe_price never matches when no price is configured" do
    Plan::UNLIMITED.stubs(:stripe_price_id).returns(nil)

    assert_nil Plan.for_stripe_price(nil)
    assert_nil Plan.for_stripe_price("")
  end

  test "stripe_price_id reads its environment variable" do
    with_env("STRIPE_UNLIMITED_PLUS_PRICE_ID" => "price_plus_from_env") do
      assert_equal "price_plus_from_env", Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS.stripe_price_id
    end
  end

  test "free plan has no Stripe price" do
    assert_nil Plan::FREE.stripe_price_id
  end

  private
    def with_env(vars)
      original = vars.keys.index_with { |key| ENV[key] }
      vars.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
      yield
    ensure
      original.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
    end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class AccountSubscriptionTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @account = accounts(:initech)
    Plan::UNLIMITED.stubs(:stripe_price_id).returns("price_unlimited")
    Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS.stubs(:stripe_price_id).returns("price_unlimited_plus")
  end

  test "creates a subscription for the account from a Stripe subscription" do
    record = AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited"), event_at: Time.current)

    assert_equal @account, record.account
    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED, record.plan
    assert_equal "cus_123", record.stripe_customer_id
    assert_equal "sub_123", record.stripe_subscription_id
    assert_equal "active", record.status
    assert_predicate record, :entitled?
  end

  test "reads the period end from the subscription item" do
    period_end = 3.weeks.from_now.change(usec: 0)

    record = AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(
      stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited", item_period_end: period_end.to_i),
      event_at: Time.current
    )

    assert_equal period_end, record.current_period_end
  end

  test "falls back to the subscription's own period end on older API versions" do
    period_end = 2.weeks.from_now.change(usec: 0)

    record = AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(
      stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited", item_period_end: nil, current_period_end: period_end.to_i),
      event_at: Time.current
    )

    assert_equal period_end, record.current_period_end
  end

  test "a plan change updates the existing subscription" do
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited"), event_at: 2.minutes.ago)

    assert_no_difference -> { AccountSubscription.count } do
      AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited_plus"), event_at: Time.current)
    end

    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS, AccountSubscription.find_by!(stripe_subscription_id: "sub_123").plan
  end

  test "a deleted subscription stops entitling the account" do
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited"), event_at: 2.minutes.ago)

    record = AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited", status: "canceled"), event_at: Time.current)

    assert_equal "canceled", record.status
    assert_not_predicate record, :entitled?
  end

  test "an out-of-order event older than the last applied one is ignored" do
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited", status: "canceled"), event_at: Time.current)

    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited", status: "active"), event_at: 5.minutes.ago)

    assert_equal "canceled", AccountSubscription.find_by!(stripe_subscription_id: "sub_123").status
  end

  test "an unknown price creates nothing" do
    assert_no_difference -> { AccountSubscription.count } do
      assert_nil AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription(price: "price_mystery"), event_at: Time.current)
    end
  end

  test "an unknown price on an existing subscription keeps its plan but still applies the status" do
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited"), event_at: 2.minutes.ago)

    record = AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription(price: "price_retired", status: "canceled"), event_at: Time.current)

    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED, record.plan
    assert_equal "canceled", record.status
  end

  test "a subscription without a known account creates nothing" do
    assert_no_difference -> { AccountSubscription.count } do
      AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(
        stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited", account_id: SecureRandom.uuid),
        event_at: Time.current
      )
    end
  end

  test "past_due stays entitled while Stripe retries payment" do
    record = AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription(price: "price_unlimited", status: "past_due"), event_at: Time.current)

    assert_predicate record, :entitled?
  end

  private
    # A Stripe::Subscription as the webhook sees it, with the fields this code reads.
    def stripe_subscription(price:, status: "active", account_id: @account.id, item_period_end: 1.month.from_now.to_i, current_period_end: nil, cancel_at: nil)
      Stripe::Subscription.construct_from({
        id: "sub_123",
        object: "subscription",
        customer: "cus_123",
        status: status,
        cancel_at: cancel_at,
        current_period_end: current_period_end,
        metadata: { account_id: account_id },
        items: {
          object: "list",
          data: [ { id: "si_1", object: "subscription_item", current_period_end: item_period_end, price: { id: price, object: "price" } } ]
        }
      }, nil)
    end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class Account::BillingTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @account = accounts(:initech)
    Plan::UNLIMITED.stubs(:stripe_price_id).returns("price_unlimited")
    Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS.stubs(:stripe_price_id).returns("price_unlimited_plus")
  end

  test "accounts start on the free plan" do
    assert_equal Plan::FREE, @account.current_plan
    assert_not @account.comped?
    assert_nil @account.active_subscription
  end

  test "comp grants the unlimited plan without a subscription" do
    @account.comp!

    assert @account.comped?
    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED, @account.current_plan
  end

  test "comp is idempotent" do
    @account.comp!

    assert_no_difference -> { Account::BillingWaiver.count } do
      @account.comp!
    end
  end

  test "uncomp returns the account to the free plan" do
    @account.comp!

    @account.uncomp!

    assert_not @account.comped?
    assert_equal Plan::FREE, @account.current_plan
  end

  test "uncomp is a no-op when the account was never comped" do
    assert_nothing_raised { @account.uncomp! }
    assert_equal Plan::FREE, @account.current_plan
  end

  test "an active subscription sets the plan" do
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(subscription_payload(price: "price_unlimited_plus"), event_at: Time.current)

    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS, @account.current_plan
  end

  test "a subscription takes precedence over a comp" do
    @account.comp!
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(subscription_payload(price: "price_unlimited_plus"), event_at: Time.current)

    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS, @account.current_plan
  end

  test "a cancelled subscription falls back to the comp, then to free" do
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(subscription_payload(price: "price_unlimited_plus"), event_at: 2.minutes.ago)
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(subscription_payload(price: "price_unlimited_plus", status: "canceled"), event_at: Time.current)

    assert_equal Plan::FREE, @account.current_plan

    @account.comp!
    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED, @account.current_plan
  end

  test "stripe_customer_id comes from the newest subscription" do
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(subscription_payload(price: "price_unlimited", id: "sub_old", customer: "cus_old", status: "canceled"), event_at: 2.days.ago)
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(subscription_payload(price: "price_unlimited", id: "sub_new", customer: "cus_new"), event_at: Time.current)

    assert_equal "cus_new", @account.stripe_customer_id
  end

  test "cancelling the account cancels its entitled Stripe subscriptions" do
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(subscription_payload(price: "price_unlimited", id: "sub_live"), event_at: 2.days.ago)
    AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(subscription_payload(price: "price_unlimited", id: "sub_gone", status: "canceled"), event_at: Time.current)

    assert_enqueued_with(job: StripeSubscriptionCancellationJob, args: [ "sub_live" ]) do
      @account.cancel!
    end

    )

    assert_equal "https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_test", url
  end

    StripeGateway.checkout_url(account: @account, plan: Plan::UNLIMITED, success_url: "https://a", cancel_url: "https://b")
  end

  test "checkout without a configured price fails before calling Stripe" do
    Plan::UNLIMITED.stubs(:stripe_price_id).returns(nil)

    Stripe::Checkout::Session.expects(:create).never

    assert_raises(StripeGateway::PlanUnavailable) do
      StripeGateway.checkout_url(account: @account, plan: Plan::UNLIMITED, success_url: "https://a", cancel_url: "https://b")
    end
  end

  test "billing portal opens a session for the customer" do
    Stripe::BillingPortal::Session.expects(:create)
      .with(customer: "cus_123", return_url: "https://app.example/settings")
      .returns(stub(url: "https://billing.stripe.com/p/session/x"))

    assert_equal "https://billing.stripe.com/p/session/x",
      StripeGateway.billing_portal_url(customer_id: "cus_123", return_url: "https://app.example/settings")
  end

  test "cancel_subscription cancels the Stripe subscription" do
    Stripe::Subscription.expects(:cancel).with("sub_123")

    StripeGateway.cancel_subscription("sub_123")
  end

  test "construct_event verifies the signature against the webhook secret" do
    payload = { id: "evt_1", object: "event", type: "ping", created: Time.now.to_i, data: { object: {} } }.to_json

    with_webhook_secret("whsec_test") do
      event = StripeGateway.construct_event(payload, signed_header(payload, "whsec_test"))
      assert_equal "ping", event.type

      assert_raises(Stripe::SignatureVerificationError) do
        StripeGateway.construct_event(payload, signed_header(payload, "whsec_wrong"))
      end
    end
  end

  test "webhook_secret is nil when unset" do
    with_webhook_secret(nil) do
      assert_nil StripeGateway.webhook_secret
    end
  end

  private
    def signed_header(payload, secret)
      timestamp = Time.now
      Stripe::Webhook::Signature.generate_header(timestamp, Stripe::Webhook::Signature.compute_signature(timestamp, payload, secret))
    end

    def with_webhook_secret(value)
      original = ENV["STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"]
      ENV["STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"] = value
      yield
    ensure
      ENV["STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"] = original
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class StripeWebhooksControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  WEBHOOK_SECRET = "whsec_test_secret".freeze

  setup do
    @account = accounts(:initech)
    Plan::UNLIMITED.stubs(:stripe_price_id).returns("price_unlimited")
    Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS.stubs(:stripe_price_id).returns("price_unlimited_plus")
    StripeGateway.stubs(:webhook_secret).returns(WEBHOOK_SECRET)
  end

  test "a signed subscription.created event subscribes the account" do
    payload = subscription_event("customer.subscription.created", price: "price_unlimited_plus")

    assert_difference -> { AccountSubscription.count }, 1 do
      post_webhook payload
    end

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS, @account.reload.current_plan
  end

  test "a plan change arrives as subscription.updated and changes the plan" do
    post_webhook subscription_event("customer.subscription.created", price: "price_unlimited")

    post_webhook subscription_event("customer.subscription.updated", price: "price_unlimited_plus", created: Time.current + 1.minute)

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal Plan::UNLIMITED_PLUS, @account.reload.current_plan
  end

  test "subscription.deleted returns the account to the free plan" do
    post_webhook subscription_event("customer.subscription.created", price: "price_unlimited")

    post_webhook subscription_event("customer.subscription.deleted", price: "price_unlimited", status: "canceled", created: Time.current + 1.minute)

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal Plan::FREE, @account.reload.current_plan
  end

  test "redelivering the same event changes nothing" do
    payload = subscription_event("customer.subscription.created", price: "price_unlimited")
    post_webhook payload

    assert_no_difference -> { AccountSubscription.count } do
      post_webhook payload
    end

    assert_response :ok
  end

  test "other event types are acknowledged and ignored" do
    payload = { id: "evt_1", object: "event", type: "invoice.paid", created: Time.current.to_i, data: { object: { id: "in_1", object: "invoice" } } }.to_json

    assert_no_difference -> { AccountSubscription.count } do
      post_webhook payload
    end

    assert_response :ok
  end

  test "a request without a signature is rejected" do
    untenanted do
      post saas.stripe_webhooks_path, params: subscription_event("customer.subscription.created", price: "price_unlimited"),
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "application/json" }
    end

    assert_response :bad_request
    assert_equal 0, AccountSubscription.count
  end

  test "a signature made with the wrong secret is rejected" do
    payload = subscription_event("customer.subscription.created", price: "price_unlimited")

    post_webhook payload, secret: "whsec_someone_else"

    assert_response :bad_request
    assert_equal 0, AccountSubscription.count
  end

  test "a signature older than the tolerance is rejected" do
    payload = subscription_event("customer.subscription.created", price: "price_unlimited")

    post_webhook payload, timestamp: 1.hour.ago

    assert_response :bad_request
    assert_equal 0, AccountSubscription.count
  end

  test "responds 500 when the webhook secret isn't configured, so Stripe retries" do
    StripeGateway.stubs(:webhook_secret).returns(nil)

    post_webhook subscription_event("customer.subscription.created", price: "price_unlimited")

    assert_response :internal_server_error
    assert_equal 0, AccountSubscription.count
  end

  private
    def post_webhook(payload, secret: WEBHOOK_SECRET, timestamp: Time.current)

class Card::CardLimitedTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest

    @account = accounts(:initech)
    @draft = cards(:unfinished_thoughts)
    @slug = @account.slug
  end

    @account.override_limits!(card_count: 1_000, bytes_used: nil)

    get card_draft_path(@draft, script_name: @slug)

    assert_response :success
    assert_select ".card-perma__notch-new-card-buttons", count: 0
    assert_select ".card-perma__account-limit-message" do
      assert_select "strong", text: /used all 1,000 cards/
      assert_select "a[href=?]", saas.account_upgrade_path(script_name: @slug), text: "Upgrade"
    end
  end

  test "members out of cards are asked to tell an admin rather than offered the upgrade link" do
    user = @account.users.create!(identity: identities(:jz), name: "JZ", role: :member, verified_at: Time.current)
    @account.override_limits!(card_count: 1_000, bytes_used: nil)
    sign_in_as :jz

    get card_draft_path(@draft, script_name: @slug)

    assert_response :success
    assert_select ".card-perma__notch-new-card-buttons", count: 0
    assert_select ".card-perma__account-limit-message", text: /Ask an admin to upgrade/
    assert_select "a[href=?]", saas.account_upgrade_path(script_name: @slug), count: 0
    assert user.persisted?
  end

  test "staff still see the create buttons when out of cards" do
    sign_in_as :mike
    @account.override_limits!(card_count: 1_000, bytes_used: nil)
    Identity.any_instance.stubs(:staff?).returns(true)

    get card_draft_path(@draft, script_name: @slug)

    assert_select ".card-perma__notch-new-card-buttons"
    assert_select ".card-perma__account-limit-message", count: 0
  end

  test "from 100 cards out the draft counts down" do
    sign_in_as :mike
    @account.override_limits!(card_count: 950, bytes_used: nil)

    get card_draft_path(@draft, script_name: @slug)

    assert_response :success
    assert_select ".card-perma__notch-new-card-buttons"
    assert_select "strong", text: "50 cards left"
  end

  test "exactly 100 cards out shows the first warning" do
    sign_in_as :mike
    @account.override_limits!(card_count: 900, bytes_used: nil)

    get card_draft_path(@draft, script_name: @slug)

    assert_select "strong", text: "100 cards left"
  end

  test "no warning while more than 100 cards remain" do
    sign_in_as :mike
    @account.override_limits!(card_count: 899, bytes_used: nil)

    get card_draft_path(@draft, script_name: @slug)

    assert_select "strong", text: /cards left/, count: 0
  end

  test "a comped account never sees the card countdown" do
    sign_in_as :mike
    @account.comp!

    assert_select "strong", text: /cards left/, count: 0
  end

  test "drafting still works when out of cards" do

  test "publishing is refused when out of cards and the card stays a draft" do

  test "publishing is allowed on a paid plan even past the free card count" do

end

class AccountSubscription < SaasRecord
  # Stripe statuses that keep the account on its paid plan. past_due stays
  # entitled while Stripe retries the card.
  ENTITLED_STATUSES = %w[ active trialing past_due ].freeze

  belongs_to :account

  validates :plan_key, :stripe_customer_id, :stripe_subscription_id, :status, presence: true

  scope :entitled, -> { where(status: ENTITLED_STATUSES) }
  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  class << self
    # Applies a customer.subscription.* event. Events older than the last one
    # applied are ignored, so out-of-order delivery can't roll a plan back.
    def sync_from_stripe!(stripe_subscription, event_at:)
      record = find_or_initialize_by(stripe_subscription_id: stripe_subscription.id)
      return record if record.stripe_event_at && event_at < record.stripe_event_at

      account = record.account || Account.find_by(id: metadata_value(stripe_subscription, :account_id))
      plan = Plan.for_stripe_price(price_id_of(stripe_subscription))
      plan_key = plan&.key || record.plan_key

      if account.nil? || plan_key.nil?
        Rails.logger.warn "[Billing] Ignoring Stripe subscription #{stripe_subscription.id}: unknown account or price"
        return
      end

      record.update!(
        account: account,
        plan_key: plan_key,
        stripe_customer_id: customer_id_of(stripe_subscription),
        status: stripe_subscription[:status],
        current_period_end: current_period_end_of(stripe_subscription),
        cancel_at: timestamp_of(stripe_subscription[:cancel_at]),
        stripe_event_at: event_at
      )
      record
    end

    private
      def metadata_value(stripe_subscription, key)
        metadata = stripe_subscription[:metadata]
        metadata[key] if metadata
      end

      def first_item_of(stripe_subscription)
        stripe_subscription[:items]&.data&.first
      end

      def price_id_of(stripe_subscription)
        first_item_of(stripe_subscription)&.price&.id
      end

      def customer_id_of(stripe_subscription)
        customer = stripe_subscription[:customer]
        customer.respond_to?(:id) ? customer.id : customer
      end

      # The period end lives on the subscription item in current Stripe API
      # versions and on the subscription in older ones.
      def current_period_end_of(stripe_subscription)
        timestamp_of(stripe_subscription[:current_period_end] || first_item_of(stripe_subscription)&.current_period_end)
      end

      def timestamp_of(seconds)
        Time.zone.at(seconds) if seconds
      end

# Which plan an account is on, and the support-side comp that grants one.
module Account::Billing
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :account_subscriptions

    set_callback :cancel, :after, :cancel_stripe_subscriptions
  end

  def current_plan
    if subscription = active_subscription
      subscription.plan
    elsif comped?
      Plan::UNLIMITED
    else
      Plan::FREE
    end
  end

  def active_subscription
    account_subscriptions.entitled.newest_first.first
  end

  def stripe_customer_id
    account_subscriptions.newest_first.pick(:stripe_customer_id)
  end

  def paid_plan?
    current_plan.paid?
  end

  def comped?
    Account::BillingWaiver.exists?(account_id: id)
  end

  def comp!
    Account::BillingWaiver.find_or_create_by!(account_id: id)
  end

  def uncomp!
    Account::BillingWaiver.where(account_id: id).delete_all
  end

  private
    # Cancelling an account ends its subscriptions. Stripe runs in a job so a
    # Stripe outage can't hold up the cancellation transaction.
    def cancel_stripe_subscriptions

    # job, after the cancellation commits, so a rolled-back cancellation keeps billing.
    def cancel_stripe_subscriptions
      stripe_subscription_ids = account_subscriptions.entitled.pluck(:stripe_subscription_id)

      ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do
        stripe_subscription_ids.each do |stripe_subscription_id|
          StripeSubscriptionCancellationJob.perform_later(stripe_subscription_id)
        end
      end
    end
end

class StripeWebhooksController < ActionController::Base

    customer.subscription.created
    customer.subscription.updated
    customer.subscription.deleted

  def create
    # Without the secret the signature can't be checked. Fail with a 500 so Stripe retries once it's configured.
    unless StripeGateway.webhook_secret
      Rails.logger.error "[Billing] STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set; rejecting webhook"
      return head :internal_server_error
    end

    event = StripeGateway.construct_event(request.raw_post, request.headers["Stripe-Signature"])

    if SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS.include?(event.type)
      AccountSubscription.sync_from_stripe!(event.data.object, event_at: Time.zone.at(event.created))
    end

    head :ok
  rescue JSON::ParserError, Stripe::SignatureVerificationError

## Billing

Hosted Fizzy has three plans. Every account starts on Free.

| Plan        | Price        | Cards     | Storage |
|-------------|--------------|-----------|---------|
| Free        | $0           | 1,000     | 1 GB    |
| Unlimited   | $20 / month  | unlimited | 5 GB    |
| Unlimited+  | $25 / month  | unlimited | 500 GB  |

Plans are defined in `app/models/plan.rb`. Only published cards count toward the Free card limit, so drafts always work. Out of cards, publishing and API creation are refused and the create buttons give way to an upgrade pitch. From 100 cards out, the card footer counts down ("50 cards left").

Stripe hosts Checkout and the customer portal. Fizzy only creates their sessions (`app/models/stripe_gateway.rb`) and receives subscription changes at `/stripe/webhooks`. Configure the Stripe webhook to send `customer.subscription.created`, `customer.subscription.updated`, and `customer.subscription.deleted` to that URL.

Environment:

* `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`: API key for Checkout, the portal, and cancellations.
* `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`: verifies webhook signatures. Without it the webhook returns 500, so Stripe retries.
* `STRIPE_MONTHLY_V1_PRICE_ID`: the Stripe price for Unlimited.
* `STRIPE_UNLIMITED_PLUS_PRICE_ID`: the Stripe price for Unlimited+.

`STRIPE_MONTHLY_EXTRA_STORAGE_V1_PRICE_ID` is no longer read. Storage now comes with the plan.

Cancelling an account cancels its Stripe subscriptions, from a job after the cancellation commits.

### Comps and overrides

Support works from `/admin/accounts`:

* **Comp** grants Unlimited to an account without a subscription. An account with a subscription keeps its subscription's plan. **Uncomp** removes the comp.
* **Override** replaces the measured card count and bytes used that limits are checked against. A blank field keeps its measured value. **Reset** removes the override.
* A per-account storage exception (`Account::StorageException`) still beats the plan's storage allowance.

EOF

# Which plan an account is on, and the support-side comp that grants one.
module Account::Billing
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :account_subscriptions

    set_callback :cancel, :after, :cancel_stripe_subscriptions
  end

  def current_plan
    if subscription = active_subscription
      subscription.plan
    elsif comped?
      Plan::UNLIMITED
    else
      Plan::FREE
    end
  end

  def active_subscription
    account_subscriptions.entitled.newest_first.first
  end

  def stripe_customer_id
    account_subscriptions.newest_first.pick(:stripe_customer_id)
  end

  def comped?
    Account::BillingWaiver.exists?(account_id: id)
  end

  def comp!
    Account::BillingWaiver.find_or_create_by!(account_id: id)
  end

  def uncomp!
    Account::BillingWaiver.where(account_id: id).delete_all
  end

  private
    # Cancelling the account ends its Stripe subscriptions. Stripe is called from a
    # job so a Stripe outage can't hold up the cancellation transaction. Jobs are
    # enqueued after the transaction commits (config/initializers/active_job.rb),
    # so a rolled-back cancellation never reaches Stripe.
    def cancel_stripe_subscriptions
      account_subscriptions.entitled.pluck(:stripe_subscription_id).each do |stripe_subscription_id|
        StripeSubscriptionCancellationJob.perform_later(stripe_subscription_id)
      end
    end
end
EOF

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order methods vertically based on their invocation order. This helps us to understand the flow of the code.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    method_1
    method_2
  end

  private
    def method_1
      method_1_1
      method_1_2
    end
  
    def method_1_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_1_2
"
}

## To bang or not to bang

Should I call a method `do_something` or `do_something!`?

As a general rule, we only use `!` for methods that have a correspondent counterpart without `!`. In particular, we don’t use `!` to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
"
}

# Hosted Fizzy plans. Every account starts on Free. A paid plan comes from an
# entitled Stripe subscription, and a comp grants Unlimited without one.
class Plan
  attr_reader :key, :name, :monthly_price, :card_limit, :storage_limit, :queenbee_short_name, :stripe_price_env

  class << self
    def find(key)
      ALL.find { |plan| plan.key == key.to_s }
    end

    def find_paid(key)
      PAID.find { |plan| plan.key == key.to_s }
    end

    def for_stripe_price(price_id)
      return if price_id.blank?

      PAID.find { |plan| plan.stripe_price_id == price_id }
    end
  end

  # stripe_price_env names the environment variable holding this plan's Stripe price.
  # A nil card_limit means unlimited cards.
  def initialize(key:, name:, monthly_price:, card_limit:, storage_limit:, queenbee_short_name:, stripe_price_env: nil)
    @key = key
    @name = name
    @monthly_price = monthly_price
    @card_limit = card_limit
    @storage_limit = storage_limit
    @queenbee_short_name = queenbee_short_name
    @stripe_price_env = stripe_price_env
  end

  FREE = new \
    key: "free",
    name: "Free",
    monthly_price: 0,
    card_limit: 1_000,
    storage_limit: 1.gigabyte,
    queenbee_short_name: "FreeV1"

  UNLIMITED = new \
    key: "unlimited",
    name: "Unlimited",
    monthly_price: 20,
    card_limit: nil,
    storage_limit: 5.gigabytes,
    queenbee_short_name: "UnlimitedV1",
    stripe_price_env: "STRIPE_MONTHLY_V1_PRICE_ID"

  UNLIMITED_PLUS = new \
    key: "unlimited_plus",
    name: "Unlimited+",
    monthly_price: 25,
    card_limit: nil,
    storage_limit: 500.gigabytes,
    queenbee_short_name: "UnlimitedPlusV1",
    stripe_price_env: "STRIPE_UNLIMITED_PLUS_PRICE_ID"

  ALL = [ FREE, UNLIMITED, UNLIMITED_PLUS ].freeze
  PAID = [ UNLIMITED, UNLIMITED_PLUS ].freeze

  def paid?
    monthly_price.positive?
  end

  def unlimited_cards?
    card_limit.nil?
  end

  def stripe_price_id
    ENV[stripe_price_env].presence if stripe_price_env
  end

  def price_label
    "$#{monthly_price}/month"
  end

  def card_allowance
    unlimited_cards? ? "Unlimited cards" : "#{ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_delimited(card_limit)} cards"
  end

  def storage_allowance
    ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(storage_limit)
  end
end
EOF

module Account::CardLimited
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  NEAR_CARD_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 100

  def card_limit
    current_plan.card_limit
  end

  def cards_remaining
    card_limit - effective_card_count if card_limit
  end

  # Out of cards means the next published card would go over the limit.
  def out_of_cards?
    card_limit.present? && cards_remaining <= 0
  end

  def nearing_card_limit?
    return false unless card_limit

    remaining = cards_remaining
    remaining.positive? && remaining <= NEAR_CARD_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end
end
# Support overrides for the card count and bytes used that limits are checked against.
module Account::LimitOverrides
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  def overridden_limit
    Account::OverriddenLimit.find_by(account_id: id)
  end

  def effective_card_count
    overridden_limit&.card_count || cards.published.count
  end

  def effective_bytes_used
    overridden_limit&.bytes_used || bytes_used
  end

  # Blank values mean no override for that field. Both blank removes the override.
  def override_limits(card_count:, bytes_used:)
    card_count = card_count.presence
    bytes_used = bytes_used.presence

    if card_count.nil? && bytes_used.nil?
      reset_limit_overrides
    else
      Account::OverriddenLimit.find_or_initialize_by(account_id: id).update!(card_count: card_count, bytes_used: bytes_used)
    end
  end

  def reset_limit_overrides
    Account::OverriddenLimit.where(account_id: id).delete_all
  end

# The only code that calls Stripe. Checkout and the customer portal are hosted by
# Stripe, so this only creates their sessions, cancels subscriptions, and verifies
# webhook signatures.
module StripeGateway
  class PlanUnavailable < StandardError; end

  class << self
    def checkout_url(account:, plan:, success_url:, cancel_url:)
      raise PlanUnavailable, "No Stripe price is configured for #{plan.name}" unless plan.stripe_price_id

      params = {
        mode: "subscription",
        line_items: [ { price: plan.stripe_price_id, quantity: 1 } ],
        client_reference_id: account.id,
        metadata: { account_id: account.id },
        subscription_data: { metadata: { account_id: account.id } },
        success_url: success_url,
        cancel_url: cancel_url
      }

      # Reuse the customer so an account that subscribes again keeps one Stripe customer.
      if customer_id = account.stripe_customer_id
        params[:customer] = customer_id
      end

      Stripe::Checkout::Session.create(params).url
    end

    def billing_portal_url(customer_id:, return_url:)
      Stripe::BillingPortal::Session.create(customer: customer_id, return_url: return_url).url
    end

    def cancel_subscription(stripe_subscription_id)
      Stripe::Subscription.cancel(stripe_subscription_id)
    end

    # Raises Stripe::SignatureVerificationError or JSON::ParserError for a bad request.
    def construct_event(payload, signature_header)
      Stripe::Webhook.construct_event(payload, signature_header, webhook_secret)
    end

    def webhook_secret
      ENV["STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"].presence
    end
  end
end
